name: Frank D. Foster
role: Superintendent of the Marquis de Mores' Medora slaughter-house
bio: Frank D. Foster superintended construction of Medora's new abattoir in January 1885 and in March was kept on as superintendent of the slaughter-house, which he called the most complete establishment of its size in the country. He brought his family from Chicago in May 1885, and in late June 1886 returned for the season with a force of butchers; by July 1 the coolers were filled with 300 tons of ice; in January 1886 he had also contracted to put up 500 tons of ice for the railroad, though the contract was given up a week later. In September 1886 he went to Chicago to meet the Marquis and on to Kansas City to look for a plant where beef could be killed all winter, and in November 1886 he appeared among Billings County's successful candidates.
